title: The Sterling Club with Fess Hill and Saul
summary: Goodwin recalls Lovett worked for Saul, the former Reno Club owner, at the Sterling Club about 1947 with pianist Fess Hill.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Charles, did you have something to say?
This is Crook Goodwin.
I think we're a little ahead of our story here. I think this time, Baby, I think you went to work for Saul out on Truman Road and Sterling.
Now what year would this be, approximately?
This would be about '44. No, it would be later than that, it would be about --
It would be after the inauguration.
Yeah, it would be about '47, somewhere along in there. Do you remember when you worked with Saul, with Jimmy Hill, and Sterling.
MR. GOODWIN: You and Fess.
Fess Hill, oh, great piano man.
Yeah, piano player.
Right.
This is the person we couldn't think of a while ago, this is the man that was playing with you at the 40, Fess Hill. Do you remember Fess?
That's right.
Cornelius, the old professor. He played with my band, before he died.
I can't remember a thing. He beats me remembering, I'll tell you.
He played his last live date with my band.
Yeah.
Crook was on it --
This was Fess Hill. He played at the new 40, he also played with you out at the Sterling Club for [Saul.] The same man who ran --
Who's [Saul?]
[Saul] that operated the Reno Club.
The Reno Club where Basie was playing.
He made Basie, had him on the air all the time. (Inaudible).
(Inaudible)
Basie, you understand, on the air --
John Hammond.
John Hammond, yeah.
Well, this was the same man that Baby Lovett was playing for out on Truman Road and Sterling.
That was the name of the room? Can't you remember the name of it.
The Sterling Club.
The Sterling Club, right.

We want to get back later on on John Hammond and the Reno Club, Jay McShan's band, Harlan Leonard's band and all those great bands of that time, and we'll get to it. Now we're up to about 1947, is that right, at the Starlight, at the Sterling Club out on the east side of town. And how long were you there, approximately?
At the Sterling Club?
With Fess Hill playing piano, the great Fess Hill.
Well, I can't remember exactly how long we were there, but I know it was at least a couple of years, I know that. Yeah, about a couple of years, yeah.
And then -- but you can't remember who else was on the band besides Fess?
More at --
Jimmy Hill. What was his instrument? Guitar man.
Froy Faul was with us too, and --
Who?
Clayborn Graves, saxophone. Yeah.
